title: Telemetry unit-drift triggered backpressure (P0) — postmortem
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-03-22 01:17 UTC Redwood hosted API experienced a P0-level degradation lasting ~55 minutes that manifested as increased request latency for non-streaming endpoints and repeated streaming session resets (5xx) for long-lived sessions. Customer-facing error rate peaked at ~3.4% 5xx and median TTFB increased from 40ms to 360ms on affected routes. Impact: ~18% of streaming sessions in the US region experienced reconnects; overall request success rate dipped by ~2.8% across the cluster.

What happened (short):
An instrumentation library bump in the telemetry ingestion path changed the timing metric "edge_queue_duration_ms" to report seconds instead of milliseconds (a unit regression). Aggregation rules and the adaptive backpressure controller in the serving runtime interpreted the inflated values as sustained high queue durations. The adaptive controller reacted by shrinking batching windows and enabling aggressive backpressure which reduced throughput and caused latency amplification and streaming session churn. Secondary effects: autoscaler downscale heuristics saw reduced throughput (because backpressure throttled producers) and began removing nodes; combined with the controller's throttling, this cascaded into transient request failures and KV cache pressure leading to 5xx.

Timeline (all times UTC, all timestamps approximate from logs/alerts):
- 01:12 — Canary deploy of instrumentation library (in ingestion service) completed (deploy triggered by INSTR-2034).
- 01:16 — Minor increase in raw telemetry values seen in ingestion cluster (no alert; metric shipped).
- 01:17 — First SRE dashboard alarms: "hostedapi.queue_duration_p90" breached SLO (pager).
- 01:18 — Adaptive backpressure controller logged mode=aggressive, shrink_factor=0.25 and started enforcing smaller batching windows; streaming controller began rejecting new ephemeral sessions with 429/5xx fallback flows.
- 01:20 — Customer-facing errors begin to rise; support receives first user reports of streaming reconnects.
- 01:25 — On-call SRE (Marcus Chen) escalates to P0; mitigation playbook executed.
- 01:30 — Temporary mitigation: adaptive backpressure disabled for affected backends (config toggle), manual scaling of serving pool +2 nodes initiated. Immediate error rate falls but latency still high.
- 01:37 — Investigation identifies discrepancy in metric units between instrumentation and aggregator (ingestion logs show unit=seconds).
- 01:45 — Rollback of instrumentation bump initiated (ingestion service) — rollback completed 01:52.
- 01:53 — Telemetry values return to expected magnitude; controller acknowledges normal queue durations and resumes normal batching parameters.
- 02:12 — Autoscaler begins rebalancing and adds nodes back to pool; KV cache warms.
- 02:15 — Post-incident monitoring shows error rate back to baseline and latency within SLO.

Root cause (detailed):
1) Primary cause: a non-breaking change in an internal instrumentation library (PR INSTR-2034) changed a timing helper that converted durations to float seconds instead of integer milliseconds. The ingestion service aggregates that metric without validating units. That created a ~1000x increase in observed values for "edge_queue_duration_ms".

2) Systemic design gaps that turned this into a P0:
- No unit/schema enforcement at the ingestion boundary. The telemetry pipeline accepted the metric with the wrong units without tagging.
- Adaptive backpressure controller has no sanity checks for sudden global metric scale shifts (no hysteresis/threshold to ignore unit-shift anomalies).
- Autoscaler heuristics used downstream throughput signals that were impacted by the controller's throttling, allowing a feedback loop that removed capacity while the system was under synthetic throttling.
- Insufficient canarying of instrumentation changes for high-cardinality timing metrics (the canary run did not include production aggregation topology).

Why the controller reacted aggressively:
The backpressure controller is configured to target queue_duration_p95 > 200ms -> shrink batching/enable backpressure. The inflated metric read ~200s instead of 200ms; controller applied maximum shrink factor. Because the controller acts cluster-wide per region, there was a coordinated reduction in batching across many nodes. That magnified per-request cpu/latency and caused streaming clients to time out and reconnect.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Disabled adaptive backpressure for affected backends (01:30) — immediate reduction in 5xx.
- Manual capacity scale-up +2 nodes to absorb increased per-request overhead (01:30).
- Rolled back instrumentation change in ingestion (01:45 -> 01:52).
- Re-enabled controller in monitored mode (thresholds restored) once telemetry normalized (02:00).
- Notified CS and posted customer-facing status update (01:35 -> 01:40).

Production impact summary (approx):
- Incident window: 01:17 — 02:12 UTC (~55 minutes take to recover to stable state).
- Peak 5xx rate: 3.4% at 01:28 UTC (baseline ~0.2%).
- Affected sessions: ~18% of streaming sessions in us-west-1/stateful pool experienced reconnects during the window.
- Estimated customer-visible requests impacted: ~120k requests (~2.8% of region traffic during the window).

Post-incident corrective actions (short-term & owners):
- SRE-1 (short-term): Add ingestion-side unit validation for timing metrics (reject/flag metrics that declare unexpected units) — owner: Diego Ramos — target: 2029-03-29 — JIRA: INSTR-2041.
- SRE-2: Add a sanity filter in adaptive backpressure controller to ignore changes > 100x instant scale for a given metric and require corroboration across multiple related signals (queue length, cpu, token throughput) — owner: Marcus Chen — target: 2029-04-05 — JIRA: SRE-8129.
- SRE-3: Modify autoscaler heuristics to avoid downscaling within 10 minutes of any controller-driven throttling event — owner: Evelyn Hart — target: 2029-04-12 — JIRA: SRE-8132.
- SRE-4: Create a telemetry canary checklist for instrumentation bumps that includes production-like aggregation test (simulate aggregator ingestion) — owner: Ravi Singh — target: 2029-03-30 — JIRA: INSTR-2043.
- SRE-5: Postmortem follow-up: audit instrumentation library PRs for semantic changes to helpers that emit metric units; add pre-merge CI unit-tests for common timing helpers — owner: Aisha Patel — target: 2029-04-02 — JIRA: INSTR-2040.

Runbook edits recommended (to be synced into the SRE runbook repo):
- Add a "telemetry unit drift" quick checklist under "hosted-api incidents": how to check ingestion logs for unit tags, quick query examples (promql) to compare multiple related metrics.
- Add an emergency toggle to pause adaptive backpressure via a single API call + audit log. Document authorized roles.
- Add guidance to avoid autoscaler downscale on strong negative throughput signals when other throttling signals are present.

Monitoring and alerting changes (immediate):
- Alert: add a guard "metric-scale-jump" that triggers when a metric jumps >100x within 5 minutes without matching CPU/throughput delta — notify SRE and block certain controllers from acting automatically. (Marcus Chen)
- Dashboard: add a correlated time-series dashboard showing raw ingestion metric distribution (p50/p95/p99) alongside controller mode and autoscaler decisions. (Evelyn Hart)

Lessons learned / notes to self:
- Telemetry is not 'just data' — it is an active control input to several automated systems. Any change to instrumentation needs strict schema/contract guarantees.
- Executors/controllers must assume metrics can be noisy or misreported and enforce sanity checks.
- Canarying instrumentation requires exercising the full aggregation & controller pipeline, not just unit tests or canary per service.
- The cascade occurred because multiple automated systems (controller + autoscaler) used interdependent signals; adding guardrails at each automated decision point reduces blast radius.

Open action items (owner / due):
- INSTR-2041: ingestion unit validation (Diego Ramos) / due 2029-03-29.
- SRE-8129: controller sanity filters + hysteresis (Marcus Chen) / due 2029-04-05.
- INSTR-2040: instrumentation library CI unit-tests (Aisha Patel) / due 2029-04-02.
- SRE-8132: autoscaler downscale guard (Evelyn Hart) / due 2029-04-12.
- INSTR-2043: telemetry canary checklist (Ravi Singh) / due 2029-03-30.

Appendix: quick forensic notes
- Ingestion logs show metric key "edge_queue_duration_ms" with value 197.2 and unit tag=seconds at 01:16:54; historically we observed values in range 0.5–250 (ms).
- Prometheus scrape of aggregated metric showed p95 ~ 224.1 at 01:17 vs baseline 34.0 (units mismatch).
- Controller decision trace: at 01:18:02 controller.v2 -> action=shrink batching window, reason="queue_p95 > 200" (value=224.1).
- Autoscaler trace: scaledown decision at 01:22 (reason: avg_tps down 18% for 3 min); context: controller-suppressed producers.

Draft notes / open questions:
- Should we add enforced unit tags at serialization level (e.g., hdr:units=ms) and fail on missing tags? Pros: immediate validation; Cons: risk of blocking older clients.
- How to coordinate canarying that includes global aggregations without causing too many pre-prod replicas? (cost vs safety)

Status: draft postmortem; seeking review from instrumentation and serving runtime leads. Next steps: incorporate feedback, file follow-up JIRA tasks, and schedule 1-hour review with product and dev leads week of 2029-03-26.

-- Aisha Patel (SRE), 2029-03-25
